- **Project Repository:** [baseball-data](https://github.com/SamBruce0904/baseball-data)

As an athlete playing baseball at New College of Florida, I have always been fascinated by the tension between old-school baseball instinct and modern tracking technology. This project explores whether the rise of tracking metrics has measurably changed outcomes across modern baseball eras.

## Data Sources

The data for this project comes from two primary sources: historical player and pitching statistics from the [Lahman Baseball Database](https://www.seanlahman.com/baseball-archive/statistics/) (accessed via the [Lahman R package](https://cran.r-project.org/package=Lahman)), and modern batted-ball tracking metrics (such as exit velocity and hard-hit rates) from MLB's [Baseball Savant / Statcast](https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/). Together, these datasets allow us to compare pre-Statcast (2005–2014) and Statcast-era (2015–2025) trends across Major League Baseball.
